"It is seen that the prosecution appears to proceed substantially on the act of re-posting the content without disclosing sufficient particulars establishing the requisite criminal intention or the other essential ingredients of the provisions invoked," the Court said. Justice Milind Jadhav Considering the accused's young age and career prospects, the Court noted the trauma she had suffered due to her arrest. “Applicant (Shaikh) has already suffered custody. That in itself for a young student is a scar which cannot be erased easily. The prosecution in case is dependent upon mere act of re-posting and nothing more with regard to the incident in question,” it observed. The accused, Khadeejah Shaikh, had re-posted contentious content on Instagram regarding the India-Pakistan conflict on May 7, 2025. However, she voluntarily deleted it within two hours and issued a public apology. Despite her corrective actions, she was arrested two days later for allegedly promoting communal enmity. However, the Court quashed the criminal proceedings, observing that Shaikh was not the original author of the post. It noted that no actual incident of communal disturbance or any other unlawful activity had taken place as a result of Shaikh's re-post. The Court also said that the criminal law cannot be set into motion merely because a particular post is perceived to be offensive, unless the conduct falls within the prohibition prescribed by law. “The mere possibility that a publication may cause displeasure or resentment cannot, by itself, constitute sufficient ground for criminal prosecution,” it added. items.title: One bite at the cherry: Henderson comes to India and finds it was already here
items.summary: Every judge recognises a certain kind of litigant. He loses on one ground and, after judgment, discovers another. When that fails, he changes the forum, recasts the relief, or presents an old controversy as a new cause of action. Litigation becomes less a means of resolving a dispute than a means of keeping it alive. The law calls this abuse of process. In Henderson v Henderson (1843) , Sir James Wigram V-C articulated a principle later developed into a broader inquiry into successive proceedings: parties should ordinarily advance matters which, exercising reasonable diligence, ought to have been raised earlier. This does not mean every omitted argument is lost forever. The question is whether a later proceeding unfairly reopens a controversy that ought to have ended. Finality is indispensable to justice, but must not defeat a genuine claim. India already has safeguards Explanation IV to Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), 1908 embodies constructive res judicata . A matter which might and ought to have been raised as a ground of attack or defence in the former suit is deemed to have been directly and substantially in issue. Order II Rule 2 CPC addresses omitted claims or relief arising from the same cause of action. The proviso to Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 similarly restricts a bare declaration where further relief was available but omitted. These provisions overlap with Henderson in purpose, but are not identical. Constructive res judicata is a statutory rule with defined conditions. Henderson , as developed in English law, addresses the wider question whether successive proceedings amount to an abuse of process. In State of Uttar Pradesh v Nawab Hussain (1977) , a dismissed police officer who had lost a writ petition later sued on a ground he could have raised earlier: that his dismissal was ordered by an authority subordinate to the appointing authority. The suit was barred by constructive res judicata . The tax law illustration is Devilal Modi v. Sales Tax Officer, Ratlam . After losing a writ challenge to a sales-tax assessment, the taxpayer sought to reopen it through another petition on additional grounds. The Supreme Court applied constructive res judicata to writ proceedings. A litigant cannot repeatedly challenge the same assessment merely by changing the grounds of attack. items.title: A press card is not a precondition for constitutional protection
items.summary: On October 15, the Supreme Court heard about 32 petitions on alleged police excesses during protests against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and the Chief Election Commissioner. One strand concerned women journalists who say male police personnel sexually harassed and manhandled them at protest sites. For the Centre, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said that the government cannot tell "who is a reel maker, and who is an independent journalist" . He also said no woman should be inappropriately dealt with by the police and objected to a blanket direction. Read charitably, this is an administrative complaint: police at a crowded protest cannot verify everyone holding a microphone. That may be true. The question is what follows from it. Justice Joymalya Bagchi said that the Court will examine the varying levels of protection available to accredited journalists, freelancers, independent journalists and influencers. If the protection should shrink to those who can prove they are journalists, it does not survive the Constitution. Rights that do not come with a card Unlike the First Amendment in the United States, the Indian Constitution has no separate fundamental right of press freedom. It is read into Article 19(1)(a). In MSM Sharma v. Sri Krishna Sinha (1959) , the Supreme Court said that the press stands on no higher footing than the citizen's freedom of speech and expression and that no privilege attaches to the press that is distinct from the freedom of the citizen. Therefore, journalists may receive protections or professional facilities justified by their work, but that cannot create general immunity from the law and cannot extinguish the fundamental rights of people who are not journalists. The early press cases follow the same logic. Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras (1950) , Sakal Papers v. Union of India (1962) and Bennett Coleman v. Union of India (1972) protected the circulation of information against indirect State restrictions. The Court guarded the communication of ideas, and not the speaker's professional title. Gathering information is the first step of speech. Recording public officials performing sovereign functions in a public place is not passive observation. It is how an audience gets to know. items.title: RPNLU Prayagraj finance controller removed after refusing VC’s ₹70,000 academic incentive
items.summary: The finance controller (FC) of Dr Rajendra Prasad National Law University, Prayagraj (RPNLUP) was removed after he refused to approve a ₹70,000 academic incentive for the Vice-Chancellor (VC) Usha Tandon , a Dainik Bhaskar report has claimed. The report from September 8 claims that the University has replaced 9 FCs in the past two years. It further claims that the latest removal, that of Siddharth S Tripathi, followed his refusal to approve a ₹70,000 academic incentive to the VC. Tripathi reportedly claimed that the VC could not be entitled to this incentive. When contacted, Tripathi refused to comment on the matter. In a telephonic conversation with Bar & Bench, the University's public relations officer (PRO) Prakash Tripathi said that the power to remove or appoint the FC rests with the State government and not the VC. A perusal of the University Act, however, reveals that the Executive Council appoints the FC in consultation with the State government. The Executive Council comprises the VC, two faculty members nominated by the VC, and various other government representatives. When asked whether the VC was drawing such an incentive and the basis for the same, the PRO last week requested for a query on email. A response to the same is awaited. The University has also been facing allegations of irregularities in its recent recruitment of 12 assistant professors. In a press note issued on August 20, it has denied the irregularities and mentioned having filed a police complaint against "defamatory" press coverage. Subsequently, the Uttar Pradesh government ordered a probe into the recruitment . More recently, on September 21, Justice Vinod Diwakar of the Allahabad High Court ordered a judicial probe into the allegations of caste-based harassment and discrimination by a faculty member at the University. Justice Vinod Diwakar However, a Division Bench of Justices Siddhartha Varma and Kunal Ravi Singh questioned the order and said that there was no occasion to order a judicial inquiry when an Equal Opportunity Cell is already in place at the University. An appeal against the order was placed before a bench headed by Chief Justice Arun Bhansali , who has recused himself from the matter. It is yet to be heard further.

items.title: Preaching religion without prior permission can lead to cancellation of OCI registration: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently held that preaching one's religion without prior permission from the Central government is sufficient grounds for cancelling a foreign national's Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) registration, even if no religious conversions take place [John Daniel Vs UOI] Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy observed that missionary activities are not limited to religious conversions and that OCI cardholders are required to obtain prior permission even to preach or spread their religion. " It is not only for conversion, but even to be a missionary preaching his religion, it is only a prior permission that is mandated, " the Court said. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy The Court made the observation while dismissing a petition filed by American citizen John Daniel, challenging the cancellation of his OCI registration by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO), Chennai, on September 4. Daniel was granted OCI registration in February 2015. He challenged its cancellation, maintaining that his visits to India were primarily to meet his 92-year-old mother and other relatives. The Central government, however, alleged that Daniel had been undertaking missionary activities in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh without obtaining the requisite permission. The authorities accused him of conducting religious meetings, preaching in interior villages and encouraging conversions to Christianity. The show-cause notice also alleged that he led the Laymen's Evangelical Fellowship International (LEFI), an organisation described by the authorities as functioning like a cult. Daniel denied these allegations. He maintained that he had never undertaken missionary activities in India, promoted religious conversions or held any position in LEFI. During the proceedings, the Central government produced posters, advertisements and internet materials relating to religious gatherings between 2017 and 2019. These included advertisements for meetings at an LEF Church in Tenali, Andhra Pradesh, and materials relating to religious gatherings at Stuartpuram village. The Court found that the material demonstrated Daniel's participation in religious congregations and public meetings across Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. Justice Chakravarthy observed that under the Central government's March 4, 2021 notification, OCI cardholders are required to obtain special permission before undertaking missionary, journalistic and certain other specified activities. items.title: Two IIULER Goa students die in motor accident; University to hold end-sems as scheduled
items.summary: Two students of the India International University of Legal Education and Research (IIULER), Goa died in a motor accident in the early hours of October 26. The University has said that end-semester examinations will go ahead as per schedule, from October 28. In an email in the early hours of October 27, Controller of Examinations Dr Abhishek Mishra said that students who feel unable to appear may choose not to. He added that no student should feel compelled to appear while in profound distress. Second-year students emailed the administration at 2:25 AM on October 27, seeking postponement of the exams to January 2027. They also asked for counselling on campus and a memorial for the two students. The email stated that several batchmates had to go to the hospital and endure an experience that no student should ever have to face. A student informed Bar & Bench that those at the hospital saw grave injuries and had to help move the bodies themselves. Many students are struggling to eat, sleep or focus, the email said. Mishra replied at 5:19 AM, urging students to appear as scheduled. He cited Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli, who carried on with their duties after personal loss and said that affected students could approach the University individually. A second email at 5:27 AM, to the wider batch, said that exams would go on for those able to appear and said that those who could not appear could appear for repeat examinations. Students said that repeat examinations are of 75 marks and require payment of fines, while regular papers are of 50 marks. They also said that no memorial had been organised as of Tuesday.

items.title: Here's what Jio Platforms paid in legal fees for its ₹30,000 crore IPO
items.summary: Jio Platforms Limited, the digital services arm of Reliance Industries, has earmarked ₹30 crore towards legal fees in connection with its ₹30,187 crore initial public offering (IPO), according to the company's prospectus dated October 24, 2026. Jio Platforms' allocation towards legal fees accounts for 6.39 percent of its total estimated IPO expenses, a higher proportion than several other major public offerings in India. For context, legal fees accounted for approximately 5.88 percent of Swiggy's IPO expenses in 2024 and 5.02 percent of Vishal Mega Mart's issue expenses in the same year. The corresponding proportion was 3.60 percent for Life Insurance Corporation of India's IPO in 2022 and 1.02 percent for Hyundai Motor India's public offering in 2024. International law firm Latham & Watkins LLP advised the company on international law. Khaitan & Co advised the book-running lead managers on Indian law, while White & Case LLP acted as their international legal counsel. The prospectus does not disclose the individual fees payable to the five firms or the proportion of the ₹30 crore allocation attributable to each mandate. The legal fee allocation forms part of Jio Platforms' overall estimated IPO expenses of ₹469.7 crore, equivalent to approximately 1.56 percent of the total issue size. items.title: Can you justify this loot? Supreme Court slams hospitals, government for 1,000% mark-up on cancer drugs

During the hearing of the matter, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta posed sharp questions to the Central government and private hospitals over massive mark-ups on essential drugs. The Court slammed the prevailing pricing regime, describing exorbitant hospital margins as "loot" and "dacoity" that prey on vulnerable patients with zero bargaining power. items.title: Non-Hindus can't enter Agamic temples without giving undertaking that they believe in the deity: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently ruled that non-Hindus cannot enter Agamic temples in Tamil Nadu without affirming their reverence for the presiding deity and agreeing to follow the customs and practices of the temple [ Thangam Venkatesh Vs State of TN ]. A Division Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and P Murugan held that non-Hindus who fail to furnish such an undertaking affirming their reverence for the temple's deity cannot enter the temple. " Even entry into the temple premises, cannot be permitted for non-Hindus who sport their religious markers and who do not subscribe their reverence for the deity concerned. This subscription (undertaking) must be in the format prescribed by the institution concerned ," the Court's October 23 judgment states. The Court contrasted such temples with institutions associated with Lord Ayyappa and Shirdi Sai Baba, which attracted devotees across religious communities. "Lord Ayyapa has devotees cutting across religions. Shirdi Sai Baba is also beyond religion. Both Hindus as well as Muslims claimed him as their own. The Bench also clarified that temple entry restrictions historically imposed on certain Hindu castes under Agamic practices could no longer withstand constitutional scrutiny. "We hasten to add that those injunctions (temple entry restrictions) will hold good in respect of non-Hindus who do not sign the undertaking," the Court said. Union of India & Ors ]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna briefly heard the matter today, when the Central government's counsel urged the Court to adjourn the case till November 2, Monday. The Additional Solicitor General (ASG) representing the Centre also assured the Court that no coercive action will be taken against Khan till then. " Lordship may keep it on Monday," the ASG said. " But I have to leave tomorrow (according to the FRRO directive) ," replied Senior Advocate Venkatesh Dhond , representing Khan. " (Court) may keep it on Monday. Nothing will happen. By way of an order passed on September 22 , the bench had ordered a complete ban on bursting firecrackers on public streets and roads during festivities, while prohibiting laser lights and high-intensity beam lights. Senior Advocate Aspi Chinoy drew attention to the lack of dedicated, recorded grievance helplines in the affidavits tendered by the administration. Advocate Joel Carlos, representing the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), submitted that noise complaints would be routed directly through the existing 24/7 disaster helpline 1916. items.title: Plea before Supreme Court against Tripura customary law allowing settlement of rape cases by paying fine
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice to the State of Tripura on a public interest litigation (PIL) petition challenging the constitutional validity of a provision of Tripura’s Jamatia Customary Laws Act, 2017, which allegedly allows rape cases to be settled through payment of a fine of up to ₹1 lakh. [Madhumita Bhattacharya v. State of Tripura and Another] A Bench of the Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought responses from the Tripura government and the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC) on the plea filed by one Madhumita Bhattacharya. The petition has challenged Section 143 of the Act, contending that it permits the private settlement and compounding of serious offences such as rape through payment of a fine of up to ₹1 lakh. The PIL has sought a declaration that Section 143 is unconstitutional and has also prayed for a direction requiring the respondents to place all relevant records concerning the Act before the Court. As per the plea, “Section 143 of the Act, read with Section 164 (Penalties and Fines), essentially places a price tag on a woman's dignity. By permitting an accused to be absolved of grievous sexual violence via financial means, the provision dangerously dilutes the line between a minor traffic offence and a heinous criminal act involving intent to cause hurt.” Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The PIL argues that the Sixth Schedule was designed to protect tribal cultural identity, social customs and land rights, but does not empower customary bodies to override national criminal laws governing serious offences. It contends that Section 143 therefore exceeds the legislative powers available under the Sixth Schedule and creates a parallel framework for dealing with rape. The plea also alleges that the provision creates an arbitrary and unconstitutional classification by denying tribal women equal protection of criminal law based on their geography and tribal affiliation, while undermining their dignity and bodily autonomy. “Severe offences like rape, murder, and dacoity are not private disputes between two individuals, but rather offences committed against the society at large,” the petition states. The PIL also refers to the Supreme Court’s decisions in Gian Singh v State of Punjab and State of Madhya Pradesh v Madanlal , contending that serious offences cannot be settled through compromises. items.title: NCLT should not become a dumping ground for retired bureaucrats: UK Chaudhary
items.summary: When the Supreme Court questions the quality of National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) judgments, it must also consider that the Chief Justice of India (CJI) or a nominee is part of the committee selecting tribunal members, NCLT Bar Association President Dr UK Chaudhary has said. In an interview with Bar & Bench's SN Thyagarajan, Chaudhary questioned accountability in NCLT appointments and spoke about judicial vacancies, inadequate infrastructure and recent amendments to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). items.title: 3 reasons why UP court acquitted Rahul Gandhi in case over calling Amit Shah murder accused
items.summary: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi was acquitted by a court in Uttar Pradesh on Monday in a defamation case over his 2018 remarks referring to Union Home Minister Amit Shah as an accused in a murder case. Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Shubham Verma said the criminal complaint accusing the Congress leader of defaming the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its office-bearers was prima facie suspicious, unnatural and uncorroborated. The judge added that the complaint appeared to have been filed merely for the sake of filing a complaint by hook or by crook and was motivated by political or other considerations. The criminal defamation case under Sections 499 and 500 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) against Gandhi was filed by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Vinay Mishra in 2018. According to the complainant, Gandhi, in a statement made during the Karnataka elections, had referred to Shah, who was then the national president of BJP, as a murder accused. Gandhi had made the following statement in Bengaluru: "People in India forget that the president of BJP is a murder accused. That's the truth. The party that talks about honesty, decency, has a person who has been accused of murder as president." Here are three major reasons given by the Court to acquit Gandhi: Political persons question each other's credibility during elections The judge said that during elections, such statements are routinely made among political persons questioning each other's credibility. "There is nothing unnatural in this; rather, it has been regarded as an indispensable feature of a healthy democracy," the Court said. Threshold not met The Court considered the settled legal position that defamation cases over statements made between political persons require a benchmark of a higher degree than ordinary cases. Considering the context in which Gandhi had made the statement, the Court found that it did not meet the higher standard/higher degree threshold required by law in the context of political persons and parties so as to bring it within the category of defamation. items.title: Journey of the controversial PMLA case in which Justice SK Kaul was asked to take the middle path
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has made a number of startling revelations in his memoirs titled Without Fear or Favour. In his book, he recounts a discussion called at the behest of then Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud and also involving Justice Sanjiv Khanna , where he was asked to take a "middle path" in the case concerning the validity of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and reconsideration of the Court's 2022 judgment in Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. items.title: Classic case of how not to investigate: Supreme Court slams UP Police again for botched murder probe
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday slammed the Uttar Pradesh Police for carrying out a slipshod and compromised probe in a murder case, terming it an egregious example of how a criminal inquiry should never be conducted [ Arun @ Deepak v. State of UP ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran censured the State police for fabricating a case without basic investigative steps. "The State Police would do well to educate their officers in the process of investigation...Six years have been erased from the life of a man on the strength of a concocted story built on mere surmises and conjectures. Not even a rudimentary investigation was carried out...The investigation and prosecuting agencies exist not merely to, and by whatever means bring in a conviction," the Bench remarked. It observed that the botched investigation put an innocent citizen’s life and liberty into serious jeopardy. "This is a classic case of how an investigation should not be proceeded with, resulting in the prosecution putting into jeopardy a person’s life and liberty...We were appalled at the manner in which the investigation was carried out," the Bench noted. It directed the Uttar Pradesh government to pay ₹6 lakh in compensation to the accused, one Deepak, who spent six years as an undertrial behind bars. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The development comes amid repeated strictures passed by the apex court against the UP Police over botched and compromised investigations. Last month, a Bench led by Justice Sanjay Kumar had remarked that the Court might as well disband the State's police force and hand over all matters to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), after flagging serious discrepancies and cover-ups in criminal inquiries. We might as well disband UP Police: Supreme Court on "cover up job", biased probe In the present case Deepak had approached the top court seeking bail after being in custody since November 2019 in connection with an FIR registered in Agra under Sections 364 ( kidnapping to murder ), 302 ( murder ), and 201 ( disappearance of evidence ) of the Indian Penal Code. Taking note of his prolonged custody in a case hinging entirely on circumstantial evidence, the Supreme Court in March this year directed the trial court to conclude proceedings within three months. items.title: Should farmers starve? Sharp exchange in Supreme Court between lawyers over  land acquisition for Ayodhya development
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday reserved its judgment on a plea challenging the acquisition of around 450 acres of land for a development scheme in Ayodhya. During the hearing, a bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Johanna observed that social impact assessment should not be brushed aside lightly, but cautioned against making it a “millstone around the neck” of the State. The hearing was also privy to sharp exchange of words between lawyers with those opposing the land acquisition flagging the impact it could have on farmers in the area. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The Court was hearing Shri Saryu Nagar Vikas Samiti’s challenge to an Allahabad High Court judgment concerning the acquisition of land under the Uttar Pradesh Awas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965. The High Court’s August 6 ruling declined to quash the acquisition but directed that landowners receive compensation, rehabilitation and resettlement benefits on the same parameters as the 2013 land acquisition law. It held that undoing the proceedings would jeopardise the public purpose, with some land already allotted to third parties. Before the Supreme Court, the Samiti argued that the 2013 law’s protections extend beyond compensation to safeguards governing acquisition itself, including social impact assessment and restrictions on acquiring irrigated multi-crop land. Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan submitted that two earlier schemes covered approximately 1,400 acres, of which only 70 acres had been utilised. He questioned the need to acquire another 450 acres without examining the availability of previously acquired land. Defending the acquisition, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati said the third phase formed part of Ayodhya’s comprehensive development, including housing, roads, schools, hospitals, hotels, mutts and ashrams. Possession has been taken in three of four villages, she said. The submissions prompted a sharp exchange over construction of hotels in the city. “How can a place like Ayodhya have no hotels?” Bhati asked. “Do not take multi-crop land for it,” Sankaranarayanan responded. When Bhati referred to global attention on Ayodhya’s development and pilgrimage, he asked, “And so let the farmers starve?” “Nobody is starving anyone,” Bhati replied, maintaining that statutory compensation and other benefits were being provided. Noida-based Twisha Sharma had married Bhopal-based lawyer Samarth Singh after the two met through a dating app. Barely five months into the marriage, Sharma was found hanging at her matrimonial home in Bhopal on May 12. items.title: Depression after spouse's death sufficient ground to condone delay in consumer complaint: Delhi Commission
items.summary: The Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission recently held that depression following the death of a spouse can constitute sufficient cause for excusing delay in filing a consumer complaint [Priya Mehrotra v. Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd.]. A Bench of Commission President Justice Sangita Dhingra Sehgal and Member Bimla Kumari made the observation while condoning a 250-day delay in a widow's complaint against Tata AIG General Insurance Company over the rejection of a medical insurance claim. The Commission accepted that the complainant's treatment for clinical depression following her husband's death sufficiently explained the delay. " On perusal of record, we find that there has been a delay of 250 days in filing the Complaint before the District Commission, for which, the Appellant has given sufficient cause, being that she was seeking treatment for clinical depression after the demise of her husband. items.title: Karnataka High Court orders crackdown on unauthorised SIM activation
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently directed the State’s Cyber Command to examine and take steps to curb the unauthorised activation and circulation of SIM cards obtained using the Aadhaar and identification details of unsuspecting individuals [ Mallikarjuna Vs State of Karnataka ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj passed the order while dismissing a plea filed by one Mallikarjuna to quash criminal proceedings intiated against him on allegtions that he possessed and attempted to sell 55 Jio and 20 Vodafone pre-activated SIM cards. The Court has asked telecom operators to strengthen customer verification before the issue of SIMs, inventory management and oversight of authorized distributors. “Pre-activated SIM cards, when circulated without the knowledge or consent of the persons in whose names they stand registered, may facilitate the concealment of the identity of the actual user and complicate the tracing of persons involved in unlawful activities,” the Court observed. Justice Suraj Govindraj By its September 29 ruling, the Court directed the Director General of Police, Cyber Command, Karnataka, to assess how unauthorised SIM activation is detected, the challenges faced by investigating agencies in identifying actual users, and measures needed to prevent the misuse of identification documents belonging to unsuspecting individuals. items.title: Supreme Court directs States to provide bar rooms, washrooms for women lawyers in all district courts
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed all State governments and High Courts to ensure that women advocates have exclusive bar rooms, washrooms and other basic amenities in district, sub-divisional and taluka courts wherever they practise, irrespective of their numbers [Sarika Tyagi v Union of India] . A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that the facilities must be created even where additional funds or land are required. “If there are no ladies’ bar rooms, we strongly disapprove of it. It is the duty of all High Courts and State governments to ensure that wherever women members, young women are practising, they are provided an exclusive women’s bar room with all facilities. This is the mandate. We do not want to deviate from that. It has to be complied with, whether additional funds or additional land are required. Whatever is required must be done,” said CJI Kant. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana Additionally, the Court directed that the facilities be provided wherever women advocates practise, regardless of their numbers. "Wherever women members of the Bar practise in district, sub-divisional and taluka courts, irrespective of their strength, a separate and exclusive women’s bar room shall be provided, proportionate to their strength, along with basic amenities such as washrooms and other facilities. We direct all State governments to allocate the necessary funds, if not already available," said the Court. It also tasked High Court infrastructure committees with prioritising the creation of these facilities in district and taluka courts. The directions were passed in a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by women advocates highlighting the lack of adequate facilities for women lawyers in court complexes across the country. The Court appointed Attorney General for India (AG) R Venkataramani as the nodal authority to coordinate compliance by States and Union Territories and consolidate their progress reports. "The pattern of basic amenities and facilities should preferably be uniform across all States," added the Court. The matter will next be heard on December 2. items.title: Called Twisha Sharma a murderer in heat of moment over abortion, didn't abet suicide: Giribala Singh to MP High Court
items.summary: Former judicial officer Giribala Singh on Monday argued before the Madhya Pradesh High Court that while she was unhappy with her daughter-in-law Twisha Sharma's decision to abort her child, she had neither subjected her to cruelty nor abetted her suicide. The submission was made by counsel representing Singh before Justice Ajay Kumar Nirankari during the hearing of her bail plea. The counsel added that had Giribala Singh and her son Samarth Singh, a lawyer, forced Sharma to abort the child, it would have caused cruelty. "The mother-in-law was very upset because the daughter-in-law was not listening to her and had gone through with the act. I would like to know which mother-in-law would be happy about this. Natural reaction would be of anger. She has expressed displeasure by not talking to her. Very natural reaction which would happen with any normal human being," the senior counsel representing Singh said. While referring to chats indicating that Singh may have called Sharma a murderer for going ahead with the abortion, the senior counsel said, "Both mother-in-law and husband wanted the child, so if she has called her a murderer, does it mean she wants her to commit suicide?" He added that it was said in the heat of the moment for which Girbala Singh later apologized. "All that Giribala has said 'murderer, murdered, murderer'... it was in the heat of the moment." Justice Ajay Kumar Nirankari The counsel further submitted that instead the chats reveal that Samarath Singh's behaviour could have caused her to die by suicide. "I submit that this clearly exonerates Giribala. Whatever is being said is being said against Samarth. I mean the reason for her committing suicide from this chat would appear that it is on account of the behaviour of Samarth that she has committed suicide ," the senior counsel said. The Court was also told that Sharma intended to live in Delhi and had applied for a job there. "It is not a case that she was in confinement. It is not a case where she could not go anywhere," the counsel said, while challenging the charge of abetment to suicide. The senior counsel also argued that bail must be granted in cases involving offences punishable with imprisonment of up to seven years. Singh's counsel today concluded their arguments. items.title: Supreme Court rejects plea against AIADMK MLAs who resigned to join Vijay's TVK
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a writ petition challenging the resignations of former All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) members of legislative assembly (MLAs) who crossed over to join the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) following the 2026 State Assembly elections. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that an elected representative resigning from their legislative seat and taking up ministerial office forms part of the standard political process. During the hearing, counsel for the petitioner pressed for judicial intervention under extraordinary writ jurisdiction, arguing that a constitutional vacuum exists within the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law). Counsel contended that legislators were actively bypassing disqualification penalties by submitting tactical resignations under Article 190(3)(b) of the Constitution and subsequently securing berths in the ruling government. Pointing to a First Information Report (FIR) already registered regarding allegations of horse-trading and inducement surrounding the crossover, the counsel submitted that the resignations could not be viewed in isolation. The Bench, however, declined to entertain the challenge under constitutional jurisdiction, emphasising the clear separation between writ remedies and criminal investigation. The development follows an earlier verdict where the Madras High Court upheld the turncoat AIADMK MLAs’ resignations and set a two-month deadline for disqualification pleas . In that ruling, a Division Bench of Chief Justice SA Dharmadhikari and Justice Arul Murugan had dismissed a petition by AIADMK Whip Agri SS Krishnamurthy contesting the Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker’s swift acceptance of the resignations of six MLAs - S Jayakumar, Maragatham Kumaravel, P Sathyabama, Esakki Subbaya, C Vijaya Bhaskar and MR Vijayabhaskar. The six legislators had defied the party whip during a confidence motion to back the Vijay-led TVK government before immediately stepping down. items.title: UP court acquits Rahul Gandhi in defamation case over remarks against Amit Shah
items.summary: A court in Uttar Pradesh's Sultanpur on Monday acquitted Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi in a defamation case over his 2018 remarks referring to Union Home Minister Amit Shah as an accused in a murder case. Gandhi was present before the court at the time of the pronouncement of the verdict by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Shubham Verma . The Court today said that the remarks made by Gandhi were not defamatory in nature. The criminal defamation case under Sections 499 and 500 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) against Gandhi was filed by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Vinay Mishra in 2018. According to the complainant, Gandhi, in a statement made during the Karnataka elections, had referred to Shah as a murder accused. Gandhi had made the following statement in Bengaluru: "People in India forget that the president of BJP is a murder accused. That's the truth. The party that talks about honesty, decency, has a person who has been accused of murder as president." Gandhi was referring to the Sohrabuddin encounter case, in which Shah was discharged by a special CBI court in 2014. In 2023, Gandhi was convicted and sentenced to two years' imprisonment by a Gujarat court in another defamation case for his remark "all thieves have Modi surname". The statement linking Prime Minister Narendra Modi with fugitives like Nirav Modi and Lalit Modi was made at an election rally in Karnataka's Kolar constituency in 2019. Gandhi, who was then a member of parliament from Wayanad, had been disqualified from parliament after his conviction in the case. However, the conviction was later stayed by the Supreme Court – the interim order enabled him to continue to be a lawmaker. According to the First Information Report (FIR) registered by the Cheranalloor police, the victim, identified as Jayabalakrishnan (55), was returning home after closing his roadside eatery when the accident occurred around 2:20 AM on Sunday morning. The car driven by the 17-year-old was travelling from Vallarpadam towards Kalamassery when it allegedly hit the scooter near a Ford showroom on Container Road. According to reports , the teenager was initially released on station bail, however, after continued protests by the victim's family and local residents, Section 105 of the BNS was also added to the case, which deals with punishment for culpable homicide, not amounting to murder. The police then took him into custody. The minor was subsequently produced before the Juvenile Justice Board today morning. The victim's family has demanded action against the teenager's father, who is the registered owner of the car. items.title: Bengaluru Court orders Kannada news channel to pay ₹1 lakh for defaming Karnataka Bank
items.summary: A Court in Bengaluru has directed Kannada news channel BTV News to pay ₹1 lakh in damages to Karnataka Bank Limited for broadcasting defamatory statements about the bank following the resignation of its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer in June 2025. [Karnataka Bank Vs BTV] Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge RY Shashidhara also directed the channel to broadcast an apology to Karnataka Bank and permanently restrained it from publishing defamatory statements concerning the bank and its officials in relation to the dispute. In the judgment delivered on October 1, the Court held that the channel had broadcast the allegations without verifying information from credible sources. " The defendant has not followed norms of journalistic conduct issued by press council of India. The defendant has not followed principles and ethics while publishing statement against plaintiff bank ," the Court added. The dispute arose following the resignation of Karnataka Bank's Managing Director and CEO Srikrishnan Hari Hara Sarma on June 29, 2025. According to the bank, an audit for the financial year 2024-25 revealed that Sarma had incurred expenditure amounting to ₹1.16 crore towards consultants and other revenue expenses beyond his delegated powers. The bank's board subsequently considered the audit findings and recommended recovery of the amount concerned. These developments were communicated to the National Stock Exchange on May 14, 2025. Sarma subsequently resigned, citing personal reasons and his intention to relocate to Mumbai. BTV News allegedly broadcast sensational and defamatory claims about Karnataka Bank's financial stability, internal administration and the safety of customer deposits without verifying the circumstances surrounding the resignation. Among the statements attributed to the channel were warnings that depositors' money could be siphoned off and that customers should exercise caution before opening accounts with the bank. The channel also allegedly suggested that there were financial irregularities and disputes among the bank's directors. In its suit before the Court, Karnataka Bank said that these broadcasts created panic among investors and depositors, forcing its directors to respond to numerous enquiries. The bank claimed that its share price, which stood around ₹207 at the close of trading on June 26, 2025, had fallen sharply following the broadcasts. items.title: J&K High Court quashes CAT order imposing ₹10,000 cost on senior advocate
items.summary: The Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court recently quashed a Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) order imposing costs of ₹10,000 on Senior Advocate Jahangir Iqbal Ganai for appearing without uniform during virtual proceedings and allegedly making derogatory remarks "about the Court" [Jahangir Iqbal Ganai V/s Mohd Amin Dar and Others] A bench of Justice Sanjeev Kumar and Justice MA Chowdhary observed that the order was passed in a complete breach of the principles of natural justice. “We have gone through the order impugned and find the same in complete breach of principles of natural justice in that a cost of Rs. 10,000/- has been imposed upon the learned Senior counsel without even affording him an opportunity of being heard and that too on a very small matter which ought to have been sorted out in the open Court,” the Court observed. Justice Sanjeev Kumar and Justice M A Choudhary The Court passed the order on Ganai's writ petition challenging the order passed by the Jammu bench of CAT on October 07. On October 13, the Court had expressed its desire to resolve the controversy through mediation and directed both members of the tribunal as well as the senior counsel to appear personally before it in chambers on October 21. However, when the matter was taken up on October 21, while Ganai was present, the tribunal members failed to appear before the Court despite repeated attempts. In the order passed later, the Court said, "It seems that the Members of the Tribunal do not wish to cooperate." The Court observed that heated exchanges between the bar and the bench during arguments are not uncommon. “However, the Bench should forebear from escalating it to the level of initiating contempt proceedings against the advocates or imposing costs on the person of the Advocates,“ the Court added. It further said that had the tribunal members displayed restraint and maturity, the unpleasant situation leading to the issuance of a contempt notice against the senior advocate could have been avoided. At the same time, the Court emphasized that advocates, particularly senior advocates, have a higher responsibility to maintain the dignity and decorum of the Court. They must ensure that minor differences in perception do not escalate into an unpleasant atmosphere of driving a wedge between the bar and the bench, it added. “Without saying much in the matter, we wish to close the matter here only,” the bench said, while quashing the tribunal order. In India, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) can explore government-backed schemes and regular business loans to meet these needs. However, the two options differ in their eligibility conditions, funding mechanisms and repayment requirements. Government programmes can provide loans through participating lenders, subsidies or credit guarantee support, depending on the scheme. Regular business loans offer another route to finance, subject to the lender's assessment and terms. MSME loan schemes support eligible businesses through specific forms of government assistance, while regular business loans provide credit under a lender's terms. A government-backed scheme does not necessarily provide a grant or interest-free loan. A credit guarantee, for example, supports eligible lenders against a portion of credit risk. It does not remove the borrower's repayment obligation. Which MSME loan schemes can businesses explore? Meeting a scheme’s general eligibility criteria also does not guarantee loan approval or receipt of every available benefit. Review the latest official guidelines and confirm the application process, funding conditions, and requirements with the relevant authority or participating lender before proceeding. items.title: Explained: What Keralam’s new Senior Citizens’ Rights Bill covers
items.summary: The Keralam Assembly, on October 26, unanimously passed the Keralam Senior Citizens’ (Care and Protection of Rights) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a legal framework for protecting the rights, dignity and social security of people aged 60 and above. The Bill provides for the registration, regulation and monitoring of senior citizen care centres, caregiver training and certification, and measures to prevent abuse and exploitation of the elderly. It also seeks to promote healthy and active ageing and ensure support to families and caregivers. The Bill also proposes dedicated protection units at the state and district levels, a public register of certified caregivers, specialised cyber cells to address fraud targeting senior citizens, a State Reserve Fund for their welfare, and penalties for offences including abuse, abandonment and the illegal possession of an elderly resident’s property. The legislation had been referred to the Finance Subject Committee for scrutiny before being taken up in the Assembly. Chief Minister VD Satheesan said the Bill focused on the care and protection of senior citizens’ rights, with its main thrust being the development of a “silver economy”. He said older people could continue to contribute to society through their experience and knowledge and lead active, productive lives. What are the key provisions of the Bill? Rights and protection The Bill is guided by six principles: dignity and respect, the best interests of senior citizens, ageing in place and home-based care, safety and social care, independence, and participation in decision-making. It guarantees senior citizens access to affordable care, safe public spaces, digital services and safety, free legal aid, and essential eldercare products such as mobility aids, hearing aids, spectacles and continence-management products at reasonable prices. Public buildings and services must provide accessible facilities, while the government must establish accessibility standards for state digital portals intended for senior citizens. These are to include simplified interfaces, large text, voice-assisted functions and high-contrast displays. The Bill also calls for digital-literacy programmes at Pakalveedu (daycare) centres and other locations. Senior citizens must be able to access government services, banking and financial services, telemedicine, information, education, income opportunities and other digital services. items.title: Why the location of a protest matters | LME 173 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: For more than three decades, Jantar Mantar in New Delhi was where people came to make themselves heard by the political establishment. It is barely two kilometres from the Parliament and the Union government’s offices. Tamil Nadu farmers came here holding skulls. Wrestlers came here demanding accountability. And even the India Against Corruption protest was held at Jantar Mantar. The location mattered. Politicians and bureaucrats could not pretend these people did not exist. Journalists did not have to travel to the outskirts of the city to find them. Ordinary commuters could see them, ask questions and understand what they were protesting about. Now, consider what happens when you move that protest away- somewhere out of sight Now, some people may ask- does the location of a protest matter? Yes, it does And that conversation goes beyond Jantar Mantar and Delhi and even the current protests against Gyanesh Kumar Across Indian cities, governments are deciding where dissent can take place, often in the name of traffic, security and public order. This change matters to all of us Let Me Explain On October 12, 2026, the Delhi Police issued a standing order de-notifying Jantar Mantar as an authorised protest venue. Under the new rules, protests in Delhi can happen at the Ramlila Maidan, the Central Business District ground in Shahdara, and Burari ground in North Delhi. The distance of Burari ground from Parliament is roughly 23 kilometres. So even if thousands of protesters gather here, the impact is very different. The same numbers can look far less significant. So practically, the right to protest remains, but the protest itself is moved out of sight. Dissent allowed in principle while less effective in practice. First, let us understand why the location of a protest matters. But before that, a quick reminder. Democracy isn't just about what the government promises. items.title: A day after Theni jailbreak, 13 out of 17 escapees apprehended
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu police have arrested 13 among the 17 remand prisoners who escaped from the District Jail at Thekkampatti in Theni district on Monday, October 26. A search is underway for the remaining four escapees. According to the Prison Department's press release issued on Tuesday, October 27, the jailbreak occurred around 10 pm, when some inmates raised an alarm claiming that a prisoner in the third block was experiencing an epileptic seizure. When the Grade II warder on duty in the block, Stalin Prabhu, entered to check on the inmate, the prisoners allegedly attacked him and attempted to escape. They subsequently confronted the guards at the main gate, snatched the keys, and opened the main entrance to flee the premises. According to preliminary reports, all 17 prisoners were lodged in the same cell. The District Jail at Thekkampatti has an authorised capacity of 200 inmates. However, 334 prisoners were housed there at the time of the incident, the Prison Department said in the release. Earlier in the day, the police had arrested five escapees, identified as Praveenkumar, Silambarasan, Raja Sikkandhar, Rajkumar, and Lingaprasath. The names of the eight who were arrested later are yet to be shared. items.title: Nearly one crore less: Karnataka final voter roll lists 4.55 crore electors after SIR
items.summary: Karnataka's final electoral roll was published on Tuesday, October 27, with 99.32 lakh fewer names than the electoral roll as of June 16, 2026. The list released by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer has 4,55,00,011 names against 5,54,32,314 names in the earlier roll, showing a decrease of 99,32,303 voters. Speaking at a press conference, Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukumar said those not included in the list could continue to apply. “The electoral roll is on continuous updation; any eligible person can continue to apply using Form 6, 7, and 8. If you have been left out of the final roll, apply using Form 6,” he said. Anbu Kumar also thanked the civic society for their help. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) was carried out across all 224 Assembly constituencies in Karnataka. Enumeration forms were generated for the 5.54 crore electors whose names were on the rolls as of June 16, 2026. Of these, 4,46,35,975 electors, or 80.52%, submitted their forms to Booth Level Officers (BLOs). items.title: Musk's outbursts explained: What an Indian licence can do for Starlink
items.summary: Starlink has had its Indian licence since June 2025. As of late October, sixteen months on, it still can’t sell anyone a connection. The latest hold-up, if Bloomberg ’s June report is right, is the Home Ministry, which has been sitting on the final security clearance since Starlink dishes turned up in the Iran war, in a country where Starlink was never licensed. Starlink calls that report misleading and says it has built a deployment model tailored for India . In early October, Elon Musk lost patience in public and blamed Mukesh Ambani . The Narendra Modi government says it is simply following process. While one camp considers Starlink a foreign threat to be kept out, the other thinks every week of delay means villages are kept offline for a tycoon’s benefit. Since the back-and-forth in the public square is bereft of context or nuance, this piece tries to provide that missing link. Its central point is simple: an Indian licence gives India a handle on the parts of Starlink that physically sit in India, but not on the satellites overhead or the software that decides whose dish works. Territorial licences don’t restrict ability It helps to picture Starlink in four parts. There are the satellites, several thousand of them a few hundred kilometres up, which pass over India whether anyone here likes it or not. There's the dish on the customer’s roof, a flat panel that steers its beam electronically to follow them across the sky. There are the gateways, ground stations that connect the satellites to the ordinary internet. And then there’s the part nobody mentions at press conferences: the network management software in SpaceX’s operations centres, which authenticates every dish, hands out capacity, and decides which parts of the map get service at all. Older satellite broadband was what engineers call bent-pipe. The satellite was little more than a mirror, bouncing your signal down to a gateway somewhere underneath it. Newer Starlink satellites also pass traffic to one another over laser links, so a signal from a dish in Ladakh can hop across several satellites before coming down at a gateway on another continent. This ability to bounce packets between satellites adds a layer of complexity. Where your traffic leaves the network is now a routing decision made in software rather than a fact of geography. items.title: SC seeks Union govt response to media body’s petition challenging data protection law
items.summary: The Supreme Court has issued notice on a petition challenging the provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, filed by the Digital News Publishers Association. “This is the first comprehensive petition by ‘legacy media’. We are the traditional, conventional legacy media. This will change the whole concept of news. If I am left to the mercy of the data principal on whether he or she will give consent, the concept of news will be gone... News has to be new. It will close down the newsroom. What’s the point if I have to ask for permission and consent?” said Senior Advocate Madhavi Divan, representing the digital wings of 21 mainstream news outlets, according to LiveLaw . Others raised similar concerns before. When the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 were notified on November 15 last year, the DIGIPUB News India Foundation said the Act and the Rules “endanger source confidentiality, hinder public-interest investigations, obstruct anti-corruption disclosures”. DIGIPUB said it had earlier submitted formal objections to the removal of the journalistic carve-out from the DPDPA, 2023 and also highlighted that Section 44(3) substitutes Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act, thereby abolishing the public-interest override and making access to information even more restrictive. Even the Editors Guild of India warned that without an explicit exemption, journalism risks being treated as personal data processing that requires consent, “thereby chilling newsgathering and hindering accountability journalism” Now, 21 news publishers, including outlets owned by Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani, have told the Supreme Court that India’s data protection law would “render investigative journalism a benign and neutered recorder of events”. The petition, filed on October 6 by the Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), calls the law’s provisions “pre-censorship which is anathema to any democracy worth its name”. Running to 698 pages, it asks the court to quash most of the contentious provisions, which take effect from May 2027. DNPA’s members include Ambani’s Network18, Adani’s NDTV , the Indian Express and Times Internet, part of the Times of India group. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana heard the matter on Tuesday.
